articles.title: Node.js Import Metrics Explained: 5 Checks for Managed APIs in Europe and US
articles.excerpt: For a startup seeking a simple managed metrics API alternative to Prometheus and Grafana, the operational constraint is not dashboard polish. It is being able to reconstruct why a scheduled import sto…
articles.body: For a startup seeking a simple managed metrics API alternative to Prometheus and Grafana, the operational constraint is not dashboard polish. It is being able to reconstruct why a scheduled import stopped producing results, even when the scheduler and worker still look alive. Short answer: a startup should prefer a simple managed metrics API over operating Prometheus and Grafana when it can preserve five signals together: scheduled runs, starts, completions, result counts, and last-success age. Keep the self-managed stack when local query control, very high event volume, or infrastructure ownership matters more than reducing operational work. For Europe and US deployments, evaluate data placement and the alert path separately from the charting experience.

articles.title: GhostAction Returns: 772 Repos Hit in New GitHub Actions Wave
articles.excerpt: Update, Oct. 9, 2026: The campaign did not stop at the end of September. On Oct. 8, a new burst hit 346 repositories in two automated sweeps lasting minutes, according to analysis published by Socket'…
articles.body: Update, Oct. 9, 2026: The campaign did not stop at the end of September. On Oct. 8, a new burst hit 346 repositories in two automated sweeps lasting minutes, according to analysis published by Socket's research team . Two compromised maintainer accounts, kitao and henrywoo, pushed a workflow named security-audit.yml into every repository they could write to, including kitao/pyxel (18,420 stars) and uber/athenadriver. The exfiltration endpoint is the same 193.32.204.199 address documented below. Socket also reports that this variant sweeps the working tree and full git history for cloud credentials, not only GitHub Actions secrets. Unlike the September wave, where most runs stalled awaiting approval, these runs executed, and Socket confirms successful exfiltration.

articles.body: Most Kubernetes tutorials show you the output you should see. You run the command, compare your terminal with the screenshot, and move on. The comparison is the weak part. Your output can look the same and your cluster can still be in the wrong state. A pod is still starting. A label matches a pod from an earlier lab. You scaled something down and forgot. Nothing in the tutorial can tell you. So every lab in my Kubernetes series ends with a verify.sh . It checks the cluster and says which check failed, with a hint. articles.title: Silent Cron Failure Monitoring: Pair Audit Logs With External Heartbeats
articles.excerpt: A customer-support pricing rule scheduled for 02:00 can fail without producing an error because the process may never start, may be skipped, or may hang before its final log statement. Short answer: r…
articles.body: A customer-support pricing rule scheduled for 02:00 can fail without producing an error because the process may never start, may be skipped, or may hang before its final log statement. Short answer: retain structured application logs for audit and cost attribution, but use an independent heartbeat monitor to detect a missed run. Neither signal can substitute for the other. Treat the pricing rollout as an idempotent state transition, and alert on the absence of its completion heartbeat rather than searching indefinitely for an error that may not exist. This distinction matters more than the vendor choice. Logs answer which rule version ran, for which tenant cohort, with what duration and outcome; a deadline-aware heartbeat answers whether the expected execution arrived at all.

That wasn't the case Tuesday morning (Oct. 13), when SpaceX launched the CRS-35 mission for NASA . A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Pad 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida at 6:35 a.m. EDT (1035 GMT), carrying a cargo variant of SpaceX's Dragon spacecraft on the company's 35th commercial resupply mission to the International Space Station (ISS). articles.title: TB 26-08 Complex Modes in Lightly Damped Structural Systems: A Two-Mode Interaction Perspective
articles.excerpt: For more information, contact Joel W. Sills, Langley Research Center, joel.w.sills@nasa.gov Download the PDF version Complex mode shapes can emerge in a linear structure even when overall damping is l…
articles.body: For more information, contact Joel W. Sills, Langley Research Center, joel.w.sills@nasa.gov Download the PDF version Complex mode shapes can emerge in a linear structure even when overall damping is low. This behavior can occur when two structural modes are closely spaced in frequency and are coupled through nonproportional damping. As the damping interaction increases, the two modal frequencies move toward one another while the mode shapes become increasingly complex. At a critical interaction level, the two frequencies coalesce. Beyond this point, the frequencies remain approximately equal while the modal decay rates separate. At very strong interaction, the mode shapes become approximately real again, but as different combinations of the original uncoupled modes.

articles.title: NASA's Perseverance Mars rover breaks interplanetary driving record — and it's far from done
articles.excerpt: NASA's Perseverance Mars rover has broken the record for the farthest distance driven on a world beyond Earth, passing its smaller cousin Opportunity.
articles.body: In a milestone achievement, NASA's Perseverance Mars rover has broken the record for most miles driven on a world beyond Earth. On Oct. 11, Perseverance hit 28.10 miles (45.22 kilometers) traveled on Mars, breaking the record previously held by NASA's Opportunity rover which went 28.06 miles (45.16 km). It took Oppy 14 years to cover all that ground; Perseverance, by contrast, has been on Mars for just 5.5 years. The new record is far from the end of Perseverance's journey, however; the mission team thinks the rover could eventually more than double the distance it's already traveled. "Our original design was only planned to last for [about] 20 kilometers of driving," Mark Maimone, a rover driver at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, told Space.com .
